Certifying f(n)=v (nonexistence of a size-(v+1) set in {1..n}) requires an EXHAUSTIVE branch-and-bound tree (DRAT-style search certificate), the expensive half.

nodes.attack: No viable attack for our tools. A flat SAT/ILP/MIS encoding is impossible (witness has >10^50 moduli). Structured local-search over Krukenberg–Gibson building blocks to nudge the min-modulus record 42→43 is conceivable but is exactly the algebraic-construction game where humans have been stuck since 2014, not a CPU-farm-shaped problem, and success is not certifiable by a cheap exact verifier. A tractable but non-record-bearing exercise would be: exhaustively compute, for tiny N and modest C, the minimal C(N) admitting an ε-almost cover with moduli in [N,CN] (ILP over LCM(N..CN) for small N where the period is enumerable) — genuine PARTIAL-exploratory work, but no established record to beat …[truncated; see source]
nodes.current_record: Headline #27: DISPROVED (Filaseta, Ford, Konyagin, Pomerance, Yu, 2007). Related finite frontier — largest known minimum modulus of a distinct covering system = 42 (D. Owens, 2014 BYU MS thesis, structured construction), improving Nielsen's 40 (2009); Krukenberg/Gibson before. Upper bound on any covering's min modulus: ≤ 616000 (Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, Tiba, 2022, "distortion method"), improving Hough's 10^16 (2015). The 42→616000 gap is closed by neither construction nor search today.
nodes.finite_object: A covering system (or ε-almost covering system) of Z with distinct moduli, congruences a_i mod n_i, with all moduli ≥ N; the "record" instance is the largest achievable minimum modulus.
nodes.verifier: Checking that a proposed system covers Z (or leaves density ≤ ε). But the natural extremal object has >10^50 moduli and an astronomically large LCM period, so there is no flat enumerable poly-time checker over a period; verification requires the recursive distributed-covering structure of the construction itself. This absence of a clean small-object exact verifier is the disqualifier for our verifier-first farm.

Not viable. Mechanically feasible but yields at best a decimal below 0.9435, which the Tao/AlphaEvolve …[truncated; see source]

UPPER-BOUND CONSTANT: h(N) ≤ √N + 0.9435·N^{1/4} + O(1), "Vector-valued smoothing for finite Sidon sets" (arXiv 2607.01169, July 2026, eight-kernel rational certificate); prior 0.97633 (Carter, Georgiev, Gómez-Serrano, Hunter, O'Bryant, Tao, Wagner with AlphaEvolve, 2025) and 0.98183 (Carter–Hunter–O'Bryant, Acta Math. Hungar. 2025). LOWER BOUND: √N(1−o(1)) (Singer / Erdős–Turán, classical).

Both parts settled ~2022-2025; $100 effectively claimed. No small-N record table for disjoint pairs exists.
nodes.finite_object: Pairs of Sidon sets in {1,...,N} with disjoint nonzero difference sets; the finite quantity is max of C(|A|,2)+C(|B|,2) at fixed small N.
nodes.verifier: Poly-time exact: verify each set is Sidon (all C(n,2) pairwise differences distinct, O(n^2)); verify (A-A)∩(B-B)={0} by hashing difference multisets and intersecting, O(n^2). Cheap. But no target record to certify against.

nodes.attack: ILP: binary x_T per triple; for each 4-set, sum of its 4 triples ≤ 3; maximize sum(x). Or SAT: C(n,3) vars, C(n,4) tetrahedron clauses + a cardinality constraint ≥ formula+1, prove UNSAT with DRAT, plus S_n symmetry-breaking. Rough compute: n≤10 minutes; n=11–13 hours-to-hard even with aggressive symmetry breaking; the Ω(6^{n/3}) near-extremal degeneracy walls it beyond that. A ~100-core farm does not change the exponential, and even a success only CONFIRMS ex(n)=formula for one more n — a curiosity that (by the same degeneracy) tells you nothing about the asymptotic frontier.
nodes.current_record: Finite lower bound = Turán's construction = A140462(n), a closed-form polynomial (a(3k)=5/2 k^3-3/2 k^2, etc.), believed exact; multiple extremal families by Brown, Kostochka, Fon-der-Flaass, Frohmader, Razborov. Asymptotic upper bound on the density π(K_4^3) ≤ 0.561666 (Razborov 2010, flag-algebra SDP; earlier Chung–Lu 0.5936). Conjectured density 5/9 ≈ 0.5556. NO published table of exact small-n ex_3(n,K_4^3) values exists (confirmed across searches). No movement 2023–2026 on the exact-value or asymptotic front via combinatorial search; only ℓ_2-norm variants (Balogh et al. 2022, 2025) and flag-algebra refinements.
nodes.finite_object: A K_4^3-free 3-uniform hypergraph on n vertices with MORE than A140462(n) triples (would disprove Turán), OR a DRAT certificate that none exists with A140462(n)+1 triples (exact upper bound at that specific n).
nodes.verifier: K_4^3-free check: for every one of the C(n,4) 4-subsets, at least one of its 4 triples is absent. O(n^4), exact, poly-time — an excellent cheap verifier. (Cost is trivial; it's the search/UNSAT-proof side that walls out.)

nodes.attack: If attempted (not recommended): seed from published contest optima, run SA / large-neighborhood local search over sets of smooth numbers {2^a 3^b 5^c 7^d}, perturbing by element swap/rescale with the exact O(n^2) objective; and an ILP over a fixed smooth-number support (binary select n of them, minimize |sum-set ∪ product-set| via indicator constraints) for exact small-n confirmation. ~100-core farm, days per n-band. Realistic outcome: reproduce, not beat, the 2016 contest values.
nodes.current_record: TWO distinct frontiers. (1) ASYMPTOTIC (the actual $250 problem): max(|A+A|,|AA|) ≫ |A|^{1270/951 − o(1)}, 1270/951 ≈ 1.3354, Bloom [Bl25] — a theorem, NOT a finite computation. (2) FINITE small-case table: OEIS A263996 = smallest |A+A ∪ AA| over n positive integers; b-file gives every term to n≈205 (a(7)=26 via {1,2,3,4,6,8,12}, etc.). Best-known constructions for n up to 1000 were produced by Al Zimmermann's Programming Contest "Sums and Products" (Nov 2015–Feb 2016, 1,639 entries), a distributed heuristic-optimization competition. No finite-side movement found 2023–2026.
nodes.finite_object: A finite set A ⊂ ℤ_{>0} of size n minimizing the sum-product functional — either R(A)=|A+A ∪ AA| (OEIS A263996) or max(|A+A|,|AA|). The verifiable witness is the explicit n-element set.
nodes.frontier: A263996 small-case table (smallest |A+A u AA| over n-sets); contest-set records
nodes.verifier: Trivial exact checker: given A, compute the multiset of pairwise sums and products, dedupe, take union cardinality. O(n^2) integer arithmetic (bignum since products blow up), microseconds even for n in the thousands. Perfect poly-time exact verifier — the strongest part of the fit.

nodes.attack: Only conceivable attack: SAT/ILP or exhaustive counterexample hunt — for small trees T (small k) encode "G on n vertices, e(G) ≥ (k-1)/2·n+1, and G avoids T" and search over n up to feasibility (~n≤20–25, k≤~8) on the CPU farm; verify any hit with the exact subgraph-iso checker. Rough compute: modest (hours–days on ~100 cores). Expected outcome: UNSAT everywhere reachable (region already covered by AKSS + small-case theorems), producing no new result. No positive-direction certificate is possible (unbounded n). Recommend NOT pursuing.
nodes.current_record: No numeric record — open conjecture. Best-known frontier: proven for large k (Ajtai–Komlós–Simonovits–Szemerédi, ~1990s announcement); large trees with near-spanning host (Reed–Stein, arXiv:2405.15733, 2024 rev. 2025); spiders (Fan–Sun, all leg lengths; Woźniak legs≤2); caterpillars (Perles, 2017); bounded-degree trees + dense hosts (1906.10219); near-diagonal k=n-1,n-2,n-3 (Woźniak), n-4 (Tiner), n=k+4 (Wang/Li 2014). No counterexample known or expected.
nodes.finite_object: A single counterexample graph G plus a specific (k+1)-vertex tree T: e(G) ≥ (k-1)/2·|V(G)| + 1 yet T ⊄ G. Finite and cheaply checkable, but almost certainly nonexistent and unbounded in n/k.
nodes.verifier: Exact and cheap for a CLAIMED counterexample: edge-count check (trivial) + subgraph-isomorphism T↪G for a fixed (k+1)-vertex tree T, poly in n via color-coding / bounded-pattern search (O(n^{O(k)}) naive, FPT in k). The verifier is fine; the problem is there is no bounded search space to run it over (n unbounded) and the positive direction has no finite certificate.

nodes.attack: The n=17 cell is CLOSED (Parsons 1975) and n=39 is CLOSED (this repository, 2026-07-16: ER_7-deletion witness, certificates/erdos-552-f39/). Remaining open cells n=42 (needs C4-free 49-vtx min-deg-7) and n=44 (51-vtx min-deg-7): polarity-deletion families ER_7/ER_8 are certified UNSAT for both — a witness needs a different construction or general SAT on the full graph space. Require the shipped codegree/degree verifier for witnesses; DRAT/LRAT for nonexistence.
nodes.current_record: Exact values known in the literature for all n <= 38 (Boza arXiv:2409.12770 table with references; e.g. f(12..17)=17..22 published 1975-2018 — OEIS A006672's b-file, stopping at n=11, is far behind the survey literature). P42 certificates for a(12..16) and the a(17) lower witness are independent machine-checkable re-derivations, not novel records.
nodes.finite_object: For fixed n, a simple red graph on m labeled vertices with no C4 and minimum degree at least m-n. Its complement then has no K1,n. Maximizing m improves the lower bound R(C4,K1,n) >= m+1.
nodes.frontier: Repository-certified: a(12..16) = 17,18,19,20,21. a(17) = 22 CLOSED (Parsons 1975: R(C4,K1,q^2+1)=q^2+q+2 at q=4; independently, the certified 21-vertex witness gives a(17)>=22 and min-degree-5 on 22 vertices needs 55 edges > ex(22;C4)=52 [OEIS A006855], so a(17)<=22). CORRECTION 2026-07-17: the earlier 'a(39)=46 NEW VALUE' claim is RETRACTED — DS1 rev.18 (Apr 2026) Table IVa lists a(39)='46-47' OPEN (lower 46 = Wu-Sun-Radziszowski 2015 Cons.5; upper 47 = Dybizbanski-Dzido); Boza arXiv:2409.12770's '/46' cell is an off-by-one wheel-convention error vs its own source. Our 45-vertex witness (certificates/erdos-552-f39/) re-derives the 2015 lower bound. Open deciders: a(39) via SAT cell (46-vtx min-deg-7: UNSAT=>46, SAT=>47); a(42) via (49,7); a(44) via (51,7). Consult DS1, not single-survey tables.
nodes.verifier: Represent the red graph. Check C_4-freeness by requiring every vertex pair to have codegree <= 1. A blue S_n is absent exactly when every blue degree is <= n-1, equivalently every red degree is >= m-n on an m-vertex complete graph. Both checks are exact and tiny for m ~ 15-45.

nodes.attack: If attempted anyway (best shot, low expected yield): target R(4,5;3) >= 36 by SAT-searching for a good 2-coloring on 35 vertices. Encoding: C(35,3)=6545 booleans (one per triple); for each of C(35,4)=52360 4-subsets a clause forbidding all-red; for each of C(35,5)=324632 5-subsets a clause forbidding all-blue (~377k clauses). Break symmetry with a structured ansatz rather than naive lex: seed a vertex-transitive/affine construction (cyclic Z_35 or GF-based, as Exoo/CDM did) so the free search is over class-colorings, then Kissat/CaDiCaL portfolio across ~100 cores with many random seeds and cube-and-conquer splitting. Similarly probe R(5,5;3) from a cyclic seed. Rough compute: days-to-weeks …[truncated; see source]
nodes.current_record: Headline (2-color diagonal, asymptotic): OPEN; gap 2^{cn^2} < R_3(n) < 2^{2^n} (Erdos-Hajnal-Rado 1965). Doubly-exp lower bound is proven only for >=4 colors (Erdos-Hajnal-Mate-Rado); the 2-color case is the missing piece and is called one of the most intriguing open problems in the area (Conlon-Fox-Sudakov, Mubayi survey). Finite sub-problem records: R(4,4;3)=13 EXACT (lower Isbell 1969, equality McKay-Radziszowski 1991 -- the first-ever exact hypergraph Ramsey value). Off-diagonal R(4,5;3): >=24 (Isbell 1983) -> >=33 (Exoo 1998) -> >=35 via SAT-constructed coloring on 34 vertices (Contributions to Discrete Math, ~2018); upper bound believed far larger. R(5,5;3) small values essentially unknown; large-n lower bounds come from algebraic 'pair/stepping-up' constructions, not search.
nodes.finite_object: The asymptotic question has NO finite witness. The in-class finite sub-problems are exact/record small values R(n1,n2;3): a 2-coloring of the triples of an m-set with no red K_{n1}^(3) and no blue K_{n2}^(3) (lower-bound witness), or a DRAT proof that none exists (upper bound).
nodes.frontier: R_3(4,5;3) >= 35 (SAT class-decomposition record)
nodes.verifier: Poly-time exact: given a coloring of the C(m,3) triples, scan all C(m,4) 4-subsets (no red K_4 = not all 4 triples red) and all C(m,5) 5-subsets (no blue K_5). O(m^5) checks, trivial. Nonexistence certifiable via SAT UNSAT + DRAT, exactly as R(5,5).

nodes.attack: (1) Build the arrowing verifier: SAT-encode "no good 2-coloring", solve with a modern CDCL solver (CaDiCaL/Kissat), emit DRAT — reuse of the exact R(5,5) pipeline. (2) Generator is the bottleneck; do NOT blind-SA unstructured graphs. Instead take the 2025 Hermitian-unital seeds (H_3 = 63v, H_4 = 208v and their triangle systems) as structured candidates, then run SAT/MaxSAT-guided vertex/edge deletion that greedily shrinks the seed while re-verifying K4-free + arrowing (UNSAT) at each step — a verifier-in-the-loop minimization rather than a global search. (3) In parallel, run the known 786 LRX graph through the same minimizer to test whether local surgery + DRAT re-cert shaves vertices. …[truncated; see source]
nodes.current_record: 21 ≤ Fe(3,3;4) ≤ 786. Upper bound 786 = Lange, Radziszowski & Xu 2012 (explicit algebraic/Ramsey-based construction; prior chain: Lu 9697 in 2007, Dudek-Rödl 941 in 2008). Lower bound 21 = Bikov & Nenov 2020 (heavy independence-number computation on (3,3)-Ramsey graphs). Graham offers $100 for N ≤ 100; Radziszowski-Xu speculate N ≤ 127. No improvement to 786 in 14 years as of July 2026.
nodes.finite_object: A finite graph G on n vertices that (a) contains no K4 and (b) arrows (K3,K3) edge-wise. Beating the record = exhibiting such G with n < 786; the lower-bound direction = certifying no such G exists on n ≤ 21, 22, ...
nodes.frontier: 21 <= Fe(3,3;4) <= 786 (Lange-Radziszowski-Xu 2012); Graham's $100 for a K4-free graph <= 100 vertices arrowing (3,3)
nodes.verifier: K4-free: trivial poly check (enumerate 4-subsets or clique-free test). Arrowing: encode "there EXISTS a 2-edge-coloring with no monochromatic triangle" as SAT (one Boolean per edge; for each triangle two clauses forbidding all-red and all-blue). G arrows iff that formula is UNSAT. UNSAT is DRAT-certifiable. Cost: one large CDCL UNSAT per candidate — comparable scale to the R(5,5) window-UNSATs we already ran; hours-to-days for a ~200-800-vertex graph, DRAT check linear in proof size.

nodes.attack: Two candidate lines, both walled. (a) Upper bounds n≥21,k=4: exhaustively enumerate combinatorial line-arrangements, prune by projective symmetry (nauty), test real/complex realizability via Gröbner bases (Maxima/PARI). This replicates the 2010 record tool; compute grows super-exponentially, no advantage from a 100-core SAT/MIS farm. (b) Lower-bound witness: optimize over R^{2n} for more k-lines than Friedman's best (n=21–25 k=4; n=16–21 k=5). Requires exact algebraic coordinates — SA/MIS/ILP over floats or a bounded grid give weaker configs than existing algebraic constructions. No realistic compute path to a new record with our toolkit.
nodes.current_record: Headline conjecture OPEN (no proof either way); best construction n^{2-c/√log n} collinear k-tuples, Solymosi–Stojaković 2013 (still o(n²), so consistent with conjecture). Finite tables: A006065 (k=4) proven optimal up to n=20, value 23 — Zhao Hui Du, distributed exhaustive incidence enumeration + Gröbner realizability, ~2010; lower-bound constructions to n=25 (Friedman; Ed Pegg n=22, 2020). A008997 (k=5) sparse, Friedman bounds to n=21.
nodes.finite_object: A point configuration in R² (equivalently an incidence/line-arrangement structure) of n points, no k+1 collinear, maximizing the count of lines with exactly k points — the orchard-type extremal config for a given (n,k).
nodes.verifier: Given n points with exact rational/algebraic coordinates: check every pair-generated line hits ≤k points (no k+1 collinear) and count lines with ≥k points. O(n²log n)–O(n³), trivially cheap. Poly-time exact — fits verifier-first, but only verifies; it does not constrain the continuous search.

nodes.attack: Only the nonexistence sub-problem is finite/bounded. Constrained-generate connected cubic graphs on n=30,32(,34) with the no-C4/no-C8 filter baked into generation (that class is extremely sparse — only 4 graphs at n=24), then test survivors for C16/C32. Extends the certified lower bound from >=30 to >=32/>=34. Rough compute: n=30 ~1–3 core-days, n=32 tens of core-days on a 100-core farm, n>=36 out of reach. The WITNESS (prize) search is unbounded — no n ceiling — and near-certainly null, so it is not a finite computation.
nodes.current_record: Any counterexample >= 17 vertices; any CUBIC counterexample >= 30 vertices — exhaustive computer search by G. Royle & K. Markström (~2004) via cubic-graph generation (genreg/nauty-style), verifying all cubic graphs on <= 28 vertices (29 impossible by parity). Sharpest near-miss: four 24-vertex cubic graphs with no C4/C8 whose only 2-power cycle is C16. Bound UNMOVED for ~20 years; all 2023–2026 progress is theoretical (P13-free graphs; Liu–Montgomery for large min degree; Carr 2026 'predominantly cubic' structure).
nodes.finite_object: A cubic (or min-degree-3) graph on n vertices avoiding every cycle length 4, 8, 16, 32, ... — either as a counterexample (witness) or certified-absent at fixed n (nonexistence).
nodes.frontier: no counterexample: verified for all cubic graphs <= 28 vertices (Royle-Markstrom ~2004); extension = exhaustive-generation certificate
nodes.verifier: For a fixed graph, detect existence of a cycle of each length 2^k <= n. In bounded-degree (cubic) graphs, C4/C8 detection is trivial and C16/C32 detection is poly-time (color-coding / bounded DP). Cost is negligible per graph; almost all graphs are eliminated by the cheap C4 test, so amortized cost is tiny. No DRAT needed — nonexistence is an exhaustive-generation certificate (genreg/snarkhunter enumeration is the proof).

nodes.attack: Encode discrepancy-≤3 as CNF: n Boolean vars (signs), cardinality/sequential-counter constraints |partial sum|≤3 over every homogeneous AP {d,2d,…,md}, dm≤n. For the WITNESS: run parallel portfolio (Kissat + CaDiCaL + SLS YalSAT) with streamliners (fix a multiplicative-like or periodic skeleton to seed structure, as Konev–Lisitsa's 'walters(k)' did) to find sat sequences at n = 20k, 40k, 80k. Incremental/assumption-based solving to climb n. Rough compute: witness-finding is embarrassingly parallel; days-to-weeks of a ~100-core farm to push well past 14k — but no tight closure. UNSAT at the true threshold is NOT attempted (infeasible DRAT).
nodes.current_record: C=1: 11. C=2 (general): exactly 1160, tight (1161 UNSAT) — Konev & Lisitsa 2014, SAT + ~13GB DRUP cert. C=3 (GENERAL): OPEN — a length-130,000 unrestricted witness published by Konev–Lisitsa has been exactly re-verified by the P42 package; the exact maximum remains unknown. C=3 (multiplicative only): exactly 127,645 (E(3)=127,646), tight — Konev–Lisitsa; this restricted subcase is distinct from the unrestricted frontier. Headline asymptotic result: Tao 2016.
nodes.finite_object: A ±1 sequence of length n with discrepancy ≤ C (every sum over {d,2d,…,md} bounded by C in absolute value). Verifier: check all (d,m) with dm≤n — O(n log n) exact, trivial.
nodes.frontier: C=3 general witness >= 130,000 (Konev-Lisitsa unrestricted witness, exactly re-verified by P42); C=2 tight at 1160
nodes.verifier: Exact and near-free: given a candidate sequence of length n, verify max over all d≤n of running prefix-sums along the d-subsampled sequence stays ≤C. O(n log n) integer arithmetic; DRAT for any UNSAT (nonexistence) step. Canonical verifier-first fit.

nodes.attack: If attempted (not recommended): to push a(65)=Y(p_65=313), run the Ziller–Morack framework — fix a per-prime residue search with the strong "reach/interval-cover" pruning and Costello–Watts upper-bound cutoffs, distributed over the farm. Realistic compute: a(64) needed Google-Cloud scale (plausibly 10^4–10^5 core-hours with the specialized code); a(65) is meaningfully harder. A ~100-core farm running a from-scratch SAT/ILP encoding would not reach even a(60) in feasible time. No credible path to a novel record with our generic verifier-first stack.
nodes.current_record: a(1..64) of A048670 exact; latest a(62)–a(64) by Andrzej Bozek, 2021, Google-Cloud-supported, via Ziller–Morack pruned exhaustive search (Costello–Watts upper bounds). No extension 2023–2026.
nodes.finite_object: A covering witness: an assignment {a_p mod p : p≤x} together with an interval [u, u+V−1] all of whose integers are congruent to some a_p. Equivalently a run of V consecutive integers each divisible by a prime ≤x. This certifies Y(x) ≥ V. Verified against the OEIS table A048670 = g(primorial) and its interval-endpoint companion A058989.
nodes.frontier: A048670 exact to a(64) (Bozek 2021, Google-Cloud pruned exhaustion); next term = pruned-exhaustion certificate claim
nodes.verifier: Lower-bound side is a POLY-TIME exact verifier: given a claimed run [u,u+V−1] and the residues, check each of the V integers is divisible by some prime ≤x — O(V·π(x)). Cheap. BUT the exact value / OEIS-table entry requires the UPPER-bound side: certify NO run of length V+1 exists over all ∏_{p≤x}p residue choices — an exhaustive/pruned nonexistence search whose cost is the whole difficulty (no compact DRAT-style certificate is standard here; correctness rests on the specialized search's completeness).

nodes.attack: Only conceivable finite task: exact MIS on the 2^n-vertex graph {A,B edge iff |A∩B|=r} for n up to ~20-22, exploiting the huge symmetry (level structure / GL-type automorphisms) to fold the search — SAT/ILP or symmetry-reduced branch-and-bound, a few core-days per (n,r). But this produces a table nobody curates (OEIS deleted it), against no record, in a regime where FrFu already gives the answer for the meaningful large-n side. Not worth farm time.
nodes.current_record: Asymptotic question PROVED: Frankl-Wilson (1981, via R^n unit-distance chromatic number) and Frankl-Rödl 'Forbidden intersections' (Trans. AMS, 1987). Exact extremal for fixed r, n large: Frankl-Füredi 'Forbidding just one intersection' (JCTA 1985) — explicit union-of-levels family (r=1 case earlier by Frankl 1977). Exact small-n table: no live record; OEIS A390645 deleted as 'too artificial' 2025-11-23.
nodes.finite_object: A family F ⊆ 2^[n] with |A∩B|≠r for all A,B∈F, of maximum size T(n,r) — equivalently a maximum independent set in the graph on the 2^n subsets of [n] with edges {A,B} whenever |A∩B|=r.
nodes.verifier: Given a candidate family F, check |A∩B|≠r for all pairs: O(|F|²·n), poly in witness size. Fatal caveat: the extremal witness has size ~2^(n-1), exponential in n, so a write-down-able-and-checkable witness exists only for n≲20-22.

nodes.attack: Only conceivable finite move: extend the Singer affine-orbit embedding check for {0,1,3,11} to prime powers q>317 on the CPU farm, hoping to FIND an extension and thereby refute it as a candidate. Compute is trivial (O(q²) per q, minutes for thousands of q). But this is (a) already pushed past q=317 and withdrawn, (b) expected to fail since experts believe {0,1,3,11} is a true counterexample, and (c) non-terminating as a proof — a negative sweep proves nothing and a positive hit is a minor note, not a theorem or prize.
nodes.current_record: Headline DISPROVED, Lean-verified: Alexeev–Mixon (arXiv 2510.19804, PNAS 2025) — {1,2,4,8} and {1,2,4,8,13} forbidden via a structural projective-plane polarity argument ruling out ALL primes (not a search); rediscovered Hall (1947) {1,3,9,10,13}. Sawin: every size-3 set extends. Smallest forbidden size s∈{4,5} OPEN. Size-4 candidate {0,1,3,11} (Mueller, MathOverflow): the finite embedding search was pushed to prime powers q≤317 by arXiv 2604.25214 (Apr 2026), which found only empirical evidence and was WITHDRAWN (May 2026) after Mueller proved strictly stronger results via Sawin's algebraic framework.
nodes.finite_object: A perfect difference set B (q+1 residues mod q²+q+1, i.e. a cyclic planar/Singer difference set of order q) containing an affine-orbit image of the size-4 Sidon set {0,1,3,11}.
nodes.verifier: Per fixed prime power q: check B's (q+1)q ordered differences hit each nonzero residue mod q²+q+1 exactly once (O(q²)), and check {0,1,3,11} lies in the translation×multiplier orbit of B (O(q²)). Cheap and exact — but only decides ONE modulus; the actual question ranges over infinitely many q with no upper bound.

nodes.attack: Only conceivable finite attack: enumerate A ⊆ [2,m] with |A|=n for small n and m up to a few dozen; for each, over all windows I of length m, ILP/exhaustively compute the minimal B ⊆ I meeting the prime-valuation cover ∏A|∏B (a covering/set-cover over prime powers), and flag any instance with minimal |B| > 2n. Rough compute: trivial CPU-minutes at small n/m, but the reachable range (m ≲ 30) is far below where any counterexample could plausibly first appear, and Erdős's own phrasing suggests none exists — so expected yield is zero. Not worth farm time.
nodes.current_record: No tracked numeric record and no small-value table (OEIS field empty). Erdős–Surányi (1959, [ErSu59]) posed it and established g(n) well-defined/finite; re-stated in Erdős 1992 ([Er92c],[Er92e]). The conjectured bound g(n) ≤ (2+o(1))n (or ≤2n) is OPEN. erdosproblems.com marks it explicitly "cannot be resolved with a finite computation." No 2023–2026 movement found in searches. (Exact best-known upper bound from ErSu59 not confirmable via available sources — but classification does not hinge on it.)
nodes.finite_object: A counterexample witness (A, I) forcing minimal valid B > 2n; finite and exhaustively checkable, but almost certainly nonexistent at reachable scale.
nodes.verifier: For a candidate lower-bound witness (A, I): exact check that no B ⊆ I of size ≤ k has ∏A | ∏B — exhaustive over 2^m subsets (m = max(A)) with trivial integer-divisibility tests. Cheap for small m, exponential as m grows. NOTE: the UPPER bound g(n)≤k has NO finite verifier — it quantifies over the infinite family of n-subsets A with unbounded max(A), with no proven a priori cap.

nodes.attack: If one insisted on the finite slice: decision SAT "∃ K_4^3-free 3-graph on n vertices with ≥m edges" — C(n,3) boolean edge vars, C(n,4) clauses forbidding any 4-set being complete, a ≥m cardinality constraint; binary-search m; UNSAT at m+1 → exact ex(n,K_4^3) + DRAT cert. Instances are small (n=16 → 560 vars, 1820 base clauses) so witnesses are easy; the cost is the boundary UNSAT proof under a large symmetry group (needs SBP/orbit-pruning), ~100-core-days for a single new n — for a value nobody tracks. Not worth farm time.
nodes.current_record: Tetrahedron K_4^3: LOWER 5/9≈0.55556 (Turán 1941 construction; exponentially-many non-isomorphic extremal families later found by Brown, Kostochka, Fon-der-Flaass, Frohmader). UPPER π(K_4^3)≤0.561666 by Razborov (flag algebras / SDP, 2010), sharpened to ~0.5615 by Baber–Talbot (flag algebras, ~2011). Gap ~0.006 still open; no closure 2023–2026 (recent work is on ℓ2-norm variants and uniform Turán density, not this). Exact ex(n,K_4^3) known only for small n; NOT in OEIS.
nodes.finite_object: For a fixed n: a maximum K_k^r-free r-graph on n vertices (an exact small-case value ex_r(n,K_k^r)), e.g. a max tetrahedron-free 3-graph on n vertices. The headline density is NOT a finite object.
nodes.frontier: 5/9 <= pi(K_4^3) <= 0.561666 (Razborov flag-algebra SDP 2010); movable claim = a better SDP dual certificate
nodes.verifier: Poly-time exact: given an r-graph, test all C(n,k) k-subsets are non-complete → O(n^k) (O(n^4) for the tetrahedron). For an exact-value optimality claim, a SAT decision "∃ K_k^r-free r-graph with ≥m edges" yields a DRAT nonexistence certificate at m+1. Cheap either way.

That yields a certified upper-bound improvement. Comp. 78:1193–1195, 2009) computed least primitive roots for ALL p < 10^12 (per Moree's Artin survey arXiv:math/0412262, sect. on g(p)=h(p)); I could not pin the exact certified range of the PRIME-primitive-root tables, so lower is the conservative self-verified 104729 — a librarian pass on P–S 2002 should lift it toward ~10^12. A meaningful new record means N > 10^12 (~3.6e10 primes to process): days-scale but standard, hence plausible not open-easy. Theory side: Heath-Brown 1986 — at least one of {2,3,5} is a primitive root for infinitely many p; full statement is Artin-conjecture-hard, no finite resolution.
nodes.quantity: largest N such that every prime 3 <= p <= N has a prime primitive root q < p (verified range of the conjecture)
nodes.witness_object: extension certificate: for each prime p in (current N, new N], a prime q < p together with the prime factorization of p-1 and the checks q^((p-1)/r) != 1 (mod p) for every prime r | p-1
nodes.witness_verifier: per prime, verify the factorization of p-1 by multiplication plus primality of its factors, then k modular exponentiations; compact, dependency-free, spot-checkable certificates (only exceptional primes with large least prime primitive root need storing — max is 107 below 10^5)

evidence.artifact: certificates/erdos-993/ -- WROM free-tree generation with counts pinned to A000055 at every order, exact independence-polynomial DP, direct unimodality test

lower.source: OUR exhaustive sweep, certificates/erdos-993/ -- all 23,522,619,475 trees on n<=30 (10.33 core-hours), which INCLUDES an independent replication of the previous frontier n<=29 (Brett Reynolds, Zenodo v3, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19100781, March 2026, 8,691,747,673 trees) -- a single-author non-peer-reviewed preprint that nobody had replayed until now

nodes.notes: n=30 alone (14,830,871,802 trees) is 1.71x the ENTIRE cumulative n<=29 workload -- not an incremental rung. Do NOT test log-concavity as a proxy: it is FALSE for trees from n=26 (Kadrawi-Levit-Yosef-Mizrachi arXiv:2305.01784 found exactly two order-26 trees unimodal but not log-concave; arXiv:2510.18826 found tens of thousands more to 101 vertices). The frontier holder is actively working this lane (repo pushed 2026-07-22, cloud compute), so a verified-to-N record here has a short shelf life; the replication half does not.
nodes.quantity: largest n for which every free tree on at most n vertices is verified to have a unimodal independence sequence
nodes.witness_object: a tree whose independence sequence is not unimodal -- storable as an (n-1)-entry parent array, about 30 bytes
nodes.witness_verifier: exact integer DP A_v=prod(A_c+B_c), B_v=x*prod(A_c); then first strict descent with no later strict ascent. No floats, no CAS

nodes.notes: State of knowledge (paraphrased from erdosproblems.com/9, edited Apr 2026): Crocker (Pacific J. Math 36, 1971) proved infinitely many such odd integers, with >> log log N of them below N; Pan (arXiv:0905.3809) improved the count to >>_eps N^(1-eps) for every eps>0. The remaining gap — from exponent 1-eps to positive density — is theorem-shaped, not witness-shaped; Erdős believed covering-system arguments cannot settle it (representable numbers exist in every infinite AP). A006286 (terms 1,2,3,128,150,252,...; b-file to 10000 terms by Chai Wah Wu) is routinely extendable but extension is not a record. No bounded finite quantity with a gap.
nodes.quantity: Upper density of the set of odd numbers not representable as p + 2^a + 2^b (p prime) — is it positive?
nodes.witness_object: none — individual non-representable odd numbers are cheap to verify (A006286 already has a 10000-term b-file) but no finite set of them moves the density question
nodes.witness_verifier: A single term t is verifiable dependency-free: for every pair 2^a+2^b < t test t-2^a-2^b for compositeness. But the open content is the density exponent, which no finite witness certifies.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: No exhaustive computation of f(n;r,k) is cited anywhere on the problem page; every listed advance (Kleitman 1968, Frankl 1987/2017, Frankl-Furedi, Bollobas-Daykin-Erdos 1976, Frankl-Rodl-Rucinski 2012, Huang-Loh-Sudakov 2012, Frankl-Luczak-Mieczkowska 2012, Luczak-Mieczkowska 2014, Kolupaev-Kupavskii 2023) is a THEOREM covering an infinite range, not a search. r=3 is fully settled. Very recent unvetted preprints attack r=4 with heavy machinery: arXiv:2605.26060 (May 2026, finite-board …[truncated; see source]
nodes.search_space_estimate: At r=4,k=3,n=13: C(13,4)=715 candidate edges, so 2^715 families; as an ILP, 715 binaries with 715*C(9,4)*C(5,4)/3! = 75,075 no-3-matching constraints -- trivially small, and the conjectured optimum is max(330, 385) = 385. At r=4,k=4,n=17: 2,380 binaries, 44,669,625 constraints. But the conjecture's hard range is n ~ (r+1)k as k grows, where the space is 2^C(n,r) with no bound at all.
nodes.smallest_untested_case: r=4, k=3, n=13 -- the smallest cell not covered by ANY range listed on the problem page (small-n side: trivial for n<kr=12, Kleitman at n=12, Frankl [Fr17] reaches only n <= 3*(4 + 1/(2*4^9)) = 12.0000006; large-n side: the best listed for r=4 is Frankl-Luczak-Mieczkowska n > 2k*r^2/log r = 69.3, i.e. n >= 70). So the listed gap for (r,k)=(4,3) is 13 <= n <= 69. The genuinely hard regime, however, is n ~ (r+1)k with k -> infinity, where nothing is finite.
nodes.statement_short: Erdos matching conjecture [Er65d]: for f(n;r,k) = max edges in an r-uniform hypergraph on n vertices with no k pairwise disjoint edges, f(n;r,k) = max(C(rk-1,r), C(n,r)-C(n-k+1,r)) for all r >= 3. Both terms are achieved by explicit constructions; Erdos-Gallai proved r=2.
nodes.upstream_handle: FALSIFIABLE (open, but could be disproved with a finite counterexample)
nodes.verdict_reason: Inverted feasibility: the cells small enough for us to decide exactly are the cells theory already owns, and the cells theory does not own are unbounded. r=4,k=3,n=13 is a 715-variable ILP we could finish in minutes -- but a counterexample there would contradict a 60-year consensus and several published theorems abutting it, and finding none reproduces nothing publishable. Push k up to reach genuinely untouched territory and the constraint count explodes (4.5e7 already at k=4,n=17) while an S_n symmetry group makes proving ILP optimality, not just feasibility, the real cost. The FALSIFIABLE tag is technically true and operationally empty: the witness, if it exists at all, lives at large k …[truncated; see source]
nodes.what_a_witness_is: CONCRETE. An r-uniform hypergraph H on n vertices (a list of r-subsets) with no k pairwise disjoint edges and strictly more edges than the conjectured maximum. At the smallest live cell that is a subset of the 715 4-subsets of [13].

nodes.known_computational_frontier: No numerical or exhaustive search reported. Direction of evidence is strongly TOWARD the conjecture being true: degree 4 is proved and Lean-checked; a full claimed proof (shtuka, Mar 2026, gradient-flow-tree strategy) received a detailed review from Terence Tao who initially rated it plausibly correct, then found and demonstrated a fatal topological gap in Proposition 12 by plotting the flow lines of z^2-1 — his conclusion was that the flow does not organise into trees at all and the whole …[truncated; see source]
nodes.search_space_estimate: Continuum with no finite shell: degree 5 gives 5 roots x 2 coords = 10 reals, minus rotation = a 9-dimensional continuum, and unlike the distance problems there is no discrete combinatorial surrogate to enumerate, because the falsifying property is metric (a geodesic length lower bound), not combinatorial. UNKNOWN as an operation count — it is not a finite search.
nodes.smallest_untested_case: Degree n = 5. Pendyala proved the degree-four case (arXiv:2606.24875, 23 Jun 2026) and reports it formalised and verified in Lean 4.22; degrees 1-3 are trivial/known. So a counterexample must have at least 5 roots.
nodes.statement_short: For f(z) = prod (z - z_i) with all |z_i| < 1, must there always exist a path of length less than 2 inside {z : |f(z)| < 1} connecting two of the roots? EHP58 proved the weaker component lemma (some component of the sublevel set contains >= 2 roots). Formalised in FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1041.lean.

nodes.verdict_reason: The worst of the four and the clearest WALL. Fails criterion 1: the finite object (5 complex numbers) does not carry its own certificate — certifying it requires a global lower bound on the geodesic distance between roots inside a semialgebraic sublevel set, i.e. proving a non-existence over an infinite-dimensional path space. Fails criterion 3 absolutely: there is no cheap exact check; the candidate-verification problem is itself a research-grade continuous-optimisation/topology problem. Fails criterion 4 by direction: two independent expert-reviewed attempts are pushing toward a POSITIVE proof, degree 4 is already closed, and the only known source of pathological lemniscate geometry (Mac …[truncated; see source]
nodes.what_a_witness_is: NOT concrete in the operational sense. A witness is a set of n roots in the open unit disk together with a PROOF that no path of length < 2 inside {|f|<1} joins any two roots. The roots are a finite object; the certifying property is an infimum over an infinite-dimensional space of paths in a semialgebraic region.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: There is essentially none, which is the notable fact here. Baek, Koizumi and Ueoro, arXiv:2411.07274 (Nov 2024), proved the AXIS-PARALLEL variant outright: g(k^2+2c+1) = k+c/k for all -k<c<k, which determines g completely -- so every remaining degree of freedom in f is tilt. Raj Singh, arXiv:2601.22163 (Jan 2026), added only an equivalence (the conjecture for all k <=> for infinitely many k <=> convergence of sum_k (f(k^2+1)-k)); explicitly no numerics. Halasz [Ha84] gives the general …[truncated; see source]
nodes.search_space_estimate: Not an enumeration: 10 squares x 4 continuous parameters (x, y, side, angle) = 40-dimensional constrained global optimisation, minus 1 for the unit-square symmetry group's discrete action. Cost of a multistart attack is bounded by choice, not by the problem -- ~10^6 restarts x ~10^3 SLSQP iterations x ~45 pair constraints ~ 5x10^10 primitive ops, comfortably one workstation. Exhaustive …[truncated; see source]
nodes.smallest_untested_case: k = 3, i.e. n = 10: is f(10) = 3? Exactly known values are only f(k^2)=k for all k (Cauchy-Schwarz, trivial), f(2)=1 (Erdos, k=1) and f(5)=2 (Newman, personal communication to Erdos, k=2). So k=1 and k=2 are settled and k=3 is the first open rung. OEIS A391490 (Terence Tao, Dec 2025) tabulates the CONJECTURED values k+a/k, not computed ones -- do not mistake its b-file for a frontier.
nodes.statement_short: Pack n squares with disjoint interiors into the unit square; f(n) = max total side length. Is f(k^2+1) = k? (Tagged FALSIFIABLE. Equivalent, by Praton [Pr08], to the full Erdos-Soifer / Campbell-Staton table f(k^2+2c+1)=k+c/k.)
nodes.upstream_handle: https://www.erdosproblems.com/106
nodes.verdict_reason: The only one of the four where criteria 1 and 3 are cleanly met and the case is genuinely tiny. A refutation of the ENTIRE Erdos-Soifer table reduces (via Praton) to ten squares in a unit square, and a candidate is checked exactly in rationals by separating-axis tests on 45 pairs plus a rational sum -- dependency-free, milliseconds, no floating point, no CAS. That is a real verifier we could ship. What holds it back from TARGET is criterion 2 in its honest form: the space is continuous, so the search is heuristic and CANNOT certify the negative. Success requires a 90-year-old conjecture to be false at its very smallest untested instance, immediately after its axis-parallel shadow was proved …[truncated; see source]
nodes.what_a_witness_is: A refutation is fully concrete and small: 10 squares (for k=3) given as centre, side, rotation angle -- equivalently 10 rational-coordinate quadrilaterals -- that pairwise have disjoint interiors, all sit inside the unit square, and have side-lengths summing to strictly more than 3. Because both the disjointness and the excess are STRICT, any genuine counterexample can be rationalised without loss, so a witness can always be presented in exact rational arithmetic.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: f(6)=17 by Szekeres-Peters (2006) at ~1500 CPU-hours over order types; re-proved by SAT in a few CPU-hours, then 10 CPU-minutes by Scheucher (2023), then 8.53 CPU-SECONDS by Heule and Scheucher (2024). The same group's machinery settled the empty-hexagon problem at 30 points (arXiv:2403.00737). For n=7 the state of the art is arXiv:2512.24061, 'Notes on the 33-point Erdos-Szekeres problem': a triple-orientation SAT encoding with 4-set convexity constraints and convex-layer anchoring, which …[truncated; see source]
nodes.search_space_estimate: Order types of 33 points: the count is 2^Theta(n log n), roughly n^(4n) = 33^132 ~ 10^200; exact enumeration exists only up to n=11 (2,343,203,071 order types, Aichholzer). The SAT reformulation has C(33,3) = 5456 orientation variables, i.e. 2^5456 raw assignments before axioms, and per arXiv:2512.24061 the realistic instances are heavy-tailed even after anchoring.
nodes.smallest_untested_case: n = 7, i.e. does some 33-point set in general position avoid a convex 7-gon? Settled below that: f(4)=5 (Klein 1931), f(5)=9 (Turan and Makai), f(6)=17 (Szekeres and Peters 2006, exhaustive computer search). f(n) is unknown for every n >= 7.
nodes.statement_short: Happy Ending problem. f(n) = least N such that any N points in general position contain a convex n-gon. Prove f(n) = 2^(n-2)+1. ($500 for a proof, $100 for a disproof; Graham offers $1000. Tagged FALSIFIABLE.)
nodes.upstream_handle: https://www.erdosproblems.com/107
nodes.verdict_reason: Confirms our existing atlas wall -- the judgement still looks right, and for a sharper reason than 'it is hard'. Note the asymmetry we should record: VERIFYING a hypothetical counterexample is trivial (C(33,7) = 4,272,048 subsets, each an exact rational convex-position test -- seconds), so criteria 1 and 3 pass. It dies on 2 and 4. Criterion 2: the search space is ~10^200 order types and the SAT encoding is heavy-tailed at 33 points. Criterion 4 is the decisive one -- this is the most heavily-swept problem in the four: Heule and Scheucher, who hold the world record on exactly this encoding family (ES(6) in 8.53 CPU-seconds, empty hexagon at 30 points), plus a dedicated 2025 preprint, are …[truncated; see source]
nodes.what_a_witness_is: A refutation is concrete and cheaply checkable: a set of 2^(n-2)+1 points in R^2, no three collinear, containing NO convex n-gon. For the first open case n=7 that is 33 rational points with no convex 7-gon. (A proof, the $500 direction, is not a finite object at all -- it is a statement for all n.)

nodes.known_computational_frontier: Szemeredi's n/3 (unpublished, given in [Er75f]) is still the record lower bound. Few-distance-set classification: Erdos-Fishburn, Discrete Math 160 (1996) 115-125 (k<=4); Shinohara, Discrete Math 308 (2008) 3048-3055 (uniqueness of the maximum 5-distance set, 12 points); Wei Xianglin, EJC 19 (2012) #P38 (g(6)=13). Directed searches on the problem itself: StijnC checked all odd n <= 250 in the concentric-regular-n-gon family (forum, 16 Oct 2025) — but under a restricted equal-distance condition, …[truncated; see source]
nodes.search_space_estimate: Continuum: 16 points x 2 coords - 4 similarity d.o.f. = 28 free reals; the discrete shell is at most 7^C(16,2) = 7^120 ~= 1e101 distance-class labelings, each needing a real-solvability decision in 28 unknowns. Roughly 90 orders of magnitude past a workstation.
nodes.smallest_untested_case: n = 16 with 7 distances. The ladder: a counterexample needs a k-distance set of size >= 2k+2, and the maximum size g(k) of a planar k-distance set is known for k<=6 — g(1..6) = 3,5,7,9,12,13. k=5 needs n=12 and g(5)=12 exactly, but Shinohara proved the maximum planar 5-distance set is UNIQUE and it is a triangular-lattice piece, which has collinear triples, so n=12 is closed. k=6 needs n=14 > g(6)=13, closed. g(7) is unknown, so the first genuinely open slot is n=16 with 7 distances. (Note: …[truncated; see source]
nodes.statement_short: Let A be n points in R^2 with no three on a line. Does A determine at least floor(n/2) distinct distances? (Part i, OPEN — a conjecture of Szemeredi, who proved it with n/3.) Part ii, the stronger per-point form, is ALREADY REFUTED and is marked `research solved` in the Lean file.

nodes.verdict_reason: Fails criteria 2, 3 and 4. (2) 1e101 labelings over a 28-dimensional continuum. (3) The two witnesses actually produced for the (easier, now-solved) part ii both required a CAS or an ITP to confirm — eigensolver flagged his own precision errors and asked for help, StijnC verified with Maple, llllvvuu verified in Lean via Aristotle. The critical radius is a root of x^3-x^2-2x+1; exact integer squared-distance checking is not available. (4) A DeepMind autonomous prover already swept this problem and produced only a construction that turned out to be 24 years old in the literature. The remaining part i is genuinely harder than the part that AI search cracked, and the obstruction is that the …[truncated; see source]
nodes.what_a_witness_is: Concrete: n points in R^2, no three collinear, whose total distinct-distance count is at most floor(n/2)-1. Equivalently a planar k-distance set of size n >= 2k+2 with no three points collinear. Real coordinates.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: Purely analytic, no computational sweep reported anywhere. Dolzhenko [Do61] f(n) <= 4*pi*n; Pommerenke [Po61] f(n) << n^2; Borwein [Bo95] f(n) << n; Eremenko-Hayman [ErHa99] f(n) <= 9.173n and n=2 exactly; Danchenko [Da07] f(n) <= 2*pi*n; Fryntov-Nazarov [FrNa09] proved z^n-1 is a LOCAL maximiser and f(n) <= 2n + O(n^{7/8}); Tao [Ta25] all sufficiently large n. Nobody has published a numerical search over coefficient space, which is itself telling.
nodes.search_space_estimate: n=3: monic cubic modulo translation (kill the z^2 term) and rotation gives p(z)=z^3+az+b with a,b in C and one residual real symmetry — about 3 free real parameters, and the region is NON-compact. Small in dimension, but the objective at each point is a certified arc length of an implicit algebraic curve, so there is no primitive-operation count to quote: UNKNOWN as a discrete search, because it …[truncated; see source]
nodes.smallest_untested_case: n = 3. Eremenko-Hayman [ErHa99] proved the full conjecture for n=2; Tao [Ta25] (arXiv:2512.12455v2, Dec 2025, 56 pp.) proved z^n-1 is the unique maximiser up to rotation/translation for all SUFFICIENTLY LARGE n. Crucially, the abstract states no explicit threshold n_0, so the residual window is not even a known finite range of n — the same ineffective-n_0 pattern we already logged on Sendov.
nodes.statement_short: For monic p in C[z] of degree n, is the length of the lemniscate {z : |p(z)|=1} maximised by p(z) = z^n - 1? Not formalised (Lean file absent — 404 in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures).
nodes.upstream_handle: FALSIFIABLE — "Open, but could be disproved with a finite counterexample"; carries a $250 Erdos prize (erdosproblems.com/114, last edited 23 Jan 2026). Previously classified WALL in our atlas.
nodes.verdict_reason: The existing atlas wall is CORRECT and got stronger since it was set. Fails criterion 3 outright: confirming a candidate means computing the length of {|p|=1} to certified precision, i.e. rigorous numerical integration with interval arithmetic on an implicit curve — the exact floating-point dependency we refuse to ship. Fails criterion 2 in spirit: the space is a non-compact 3-real-parameter continuum at n=3 and a 2n-parameter one in general, and Fryntov-Nazarov already proved z^n-1 is a local maximiser, so any counterexample is a distant competing local max that local search will not stumble onto. And the payoff is nil: Tao closed all large n in Dec 2025 with an unstated n_0, so even a …[truncated; see source]
nodes.what_a_witness_is: Semi-concrete: a single monic polynomial of degree n whose lemniscate is LONGER than that of z^n-1. Finitely many complex coefficients — but the discriminating quantity is an arc length, a transcendental integral, not a combinatorial count.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: No exhaustive computational search found in the literature. The frontier is analytic: Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp [EFRS94] proved it with 50 replaced by 16; Krivelevich [Kr95] with n/2 replaced by 3n/5 and 50 by 25; Keevash–Sudakov [KeSu06] under e(G) <= n^2/12 or e(G) >= n^2/5; Norin–Yepremyan [NoYe15] for e(G) >= (1/5 - c)n^2; Razborov [Ra22], by flag algebras, proved it with 1/50 replaced by 27/1024 ≈ 0.026367, and proved the full conjecture for girth-5 graphs, graphs of bounded …[truncated; see source]
nodes.search_space_estimate: Triangle-free graphs on n vertices (OEIS A006785): n=14 -> 4.68e8, n=15 -> 1.42e10, n=16 -> 5.81e11, n=17 -> 3.17e13. Verifying one candidate costs C(n, floor(n/2)) subset evaluations: C(16,8) = 12,870. A full n=16 sweep = 5.81e11 * 1.29e4 ≈ 7.5e15 primitive ops — about 10^4 times over budget. And the only n small enough to sweep (n <= 14, ≈1.6e12 ops) sit in the regime where n^2/50 < 4 and the …[truncated; see source]
nodes.smallest_untested_case: There is no meaningful smallest case: the problem's content is asymptotic. The extremal families meet the bound EXACTLY at every n, not just in the limit. For C5[t] on n = 5t vertices, taking two non-adjacent classes whole (2t vertices) plus t/2 vertices from a class adjacent to exactly one of them costs (t/2)*t = t^2/2 = n^2/50 edges — exactly the threshold, and the hypothesis demands strictly more. So the whole small-n regime is pinned to the bound and no perturbation of a blow-up can win. …[truncated; see source]
nodes.statement_short: Erdős–Rousseau: if G on n vertices has the property that every induced subgraph on >= floor(n/2) vertices spans more than n^2/50 edges, must G contain a triangle? Equivalently (Razborov's phrasing): every triangle-free n-vertex graph has an induced subgraph on n/2 vertices with at most n^2/50 edges.
nodes.upstream_handle: FALSIFIABLE — "Open, but could be disproved with a finite counterexample." ($250 prize; erdosproblems.com/128, last edited 31 Oct 2025)
nodes.verdict_reason: PRIOR ATLAS WALL CONFIRMED — and for a stronger reason than headcount. Criterion 2 fails (7.5e15 ops at the first out-of-reach size) and criterion 3 fails: certifying a witness needs the exact MINIMUM number of edges over all floor(n/2)-subsets, which is the minimum-edge-k-subgraph problem — NP-hard, so an exact certificate needs an ILP/branch-and-bound, not a dependency-free checker, for any n past ~34. The killer is structural, not computational: the extremal family hits n^2/50 exactly at every n, so a counterexample must strictly beat a tight family in the regime where Razborov's flag-algebra bound already squeezes the constant to [0.02, 0.02637]. Nothing an enumerable graph can do …[truncated; see source]
nodes.what_a_witness_is: CONCRETE but expensive to certify. A triangle-free graph G on n vertices such that min over all S with |S| = floor(n/2) of e(G[S]) is strictly greater than n^2/50. The witness is an adjacency matrix; the certificate that it IS a witness requires a proven MINIMUM over all half-subsets.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: No published exhaustive search over general graphs was found. The only exhaustive search located is Puleo (arXiv:1308.2211v3, European J. Combin. 2015, Section 3): a geng run with a custom pruning function for his forbidden configurations, restricted to genus <= 2, which "identified a set of only 5299 graphs that contains any smallest counterexample of genus 2", and he notes "for higher gamma, this computational approach quickly becomes intractible". The frontier is otherwise structural: Puleo …[truncated; see source]
nodes.search_space_estimate: OEIS A000088: 274,668 graphs on 9 vertices, 1.20e7 on 10, 1.02e9 on 11, 1.65e11 on 12. The two cheap structural filters bite hard: minimum degree >= 5, and mad >= 7 forces a very dense chunk (a K8, or a 9-subgraph with >= 32 of 36 edges, or an 11-vertex graph with >= 39 of 55). At n = 11 that plausibly leaves ~1e6-1e7 candidates, each needing an exact integer tau/nu branch-and-bound at ~1-10 ms: …[truncated; see source]
nodes.smallest_untested_case: n = 9 is the first order that requires any enumeration at all: Puleo proved the conjecture whenever mad(G) < 7, and every graph on <= 7 vertices has mad <= 6, while on 8 vertices only K8 reaches mad = 7 (and K8 has tau = 12 <= 2*nu = 16). The first order where enumeration is nontrivial — and where I could find no published sweep — is n = 11 or n = 12.
nodes.statement_short: Tuza's conjecture: if G has at most k pairwise edge-disjoint triangles, can G be made triangle-free by deleting at most 2k edges? I.e. tau(G) <= 2*nu(G), where nu is the maximum edge-disjoint triangle packing and tau the minimum triangle edge-transversal. K4 and K5 show 2 is best possible.
nodes.upstream_handle: FALSIFIABLE — "Open, but could be disproved with a finite counterexample." (no prize listed; erdosproblems.com/167, last edited 13 Oct 2025)
nodes.verdict_reason: The softest of the five, and the only one not previously triaged by us. Criteria 1 and 3 pass cleanly — the witness is a graph and both tau and nu are exact integer optimisations a dependency-free branch-and-bound can settle for small n. Criterion 2 passes at n = 11 and marginally at n = 12 after the min-degree-5 and mad>=7 filters. Criterion 4 is the honest doubt: I found NO published general-graph sweep, but absence of publication on a famous conjecture is weak evidence — a null result at n <= 12 is exactly the kind of thing people run and never write up, so we would risk reproducing folklore. And the deliverable is only a table cell ("no counterexample on <= 12 vertices, certified"), not …[truncated; see source]
nodes.what_a_witness_is: CONCRETE, with a two-sided certificate. A graph G with tau(G) > 2*nu(G), shipped as an adjacency matrix plus (a) an explicit edge-disjoint triangle packing of size nu together with a proof of maximality, and (b) a proof that no edge set of size 2*nu hits every triangle. Both halves are pure-integer combinatorial optimisations — exact branch-and-bound, no floating point, no CAS. On <= 30 vertices this is seconds per candidate.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: Hindman 1981 [Hi81]: all hypergraphs with at most 10 vertices (in fact whenever the >=3-element edges span <=10 vertices). Romero & Alonso-Pecina 2014, Discrete Math. Algorithms Appl. 6(3):1450039, title literally "The Erdos-Faber-Lovasz conjecture is true for n <= 12", built on Betten & Betten's enumeration of linear spaces on <=12 points. nodes.search_space_estimate: The number of triangle-free graphs on n vertices is 2^(n^2/4 + o(n^2)). At n=205: 2^10506 ~ 10^3163. Even discounting Ferudun and taking n=25: 2^156 ~ 10^47 — already ~30 orders of magnitude past the n=17 enumeration frontier.
nodes.smallest_untested_case: 5n = 205 vertices (k=41), given Ferudun's claim that a(5k)=k^2 for k<=40. Discounting that claim, the smallest multiple of 5 not settled by exhaustive computation is 5n = 25 vertices (McKay's exhaustive frontier is n=23 vertices).

Discount it entirely (we should — our own vetting pattern this month was 5 of 6 external claims with sound math and broken verification) and the smallest open case is 25 vertices, still 10^47 graphs against an enumeration frontier of 17 vertices reached by McKay. Separately, condition 3 fails outright: a candidate counterexample cannot be cheaply certified, because proving the deletion number is large is an exact max-cut *upper* bound, …[truncated; see source]
nodes.what_a_witness_is: CONCRETE as an object: a triangle-free graph G on 5n vertices whose bipartization number (edges minus max-cut) exceeds n^2. But the object is only half a witness — certifying it requires proving max-cut(G) < e(G) - n^2, i.e. an exact max-cut upper bound on a 5n-vertex graph, which is NP-hard and at n>=41 (205 vertices) not tractable exactly.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: Verified for all n <= 10^18 [MiDu25], cited in the erdosproblems remarks. Prior partial results: Obláth [Ob50] (n+1 divisible by a prime 3 mod 4), Mordell [Mo69] (6 bad classes mod 840), Terzi [Te71] (198 bad classes mod 120120), Vaughan [Va70] exception count <= x·exp(-c(log x)^{2/3}), Elsholtz–Tao [ElTa13] f(p) <= p^{3/5+o(1)}.
nodes.search_space_estimate: One decade past the record: pi(10^19)-pi(10^18) ~ 2.05e17 primes x (198/120120 = 0.165% surviving Terzi) ~ 3.4e14 candidate n, each needing its own divisor search over x in (n/4, 3n/4] — >= 3.4e14 heavy checks vs a ~1e12 op budget.
nodes.smallest_untested_case: n prime, n > 10^18, restricted to n in one of Terzi's 198 bad residue classes mod 120120 (equivalently n = 1,121,169,289,361,529 mod 840 after Mordell). Smallest concrete untested n is the least prime above 10^18 in those classes.

nodes.verdict_reason: Frontier is already 10^18 and 100+ years of congruence sieving has removed 99.8% of n, so every remaining case is by construction a hard one. Extending by even one decade needs ~3.4e14 individual exhaustive searches, ~300x over budget before per-case cost. Worse, a positive witness is not a small object: refuting one n requires certifying an exhaustive divisor search, so criterion 3 (cheap exact verification of a witness) fails outright.
nodes.what_a_witness_is: A single integer n>2 (WLOG prime) together with a certified exhaustive search showing no (x,y,z) works. The witness is really the *exhaustion*, not the number: 'no solution' for one n is itself a nontrivial finite check over divisors of n·x.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: No computational bound is recorded anywhere upstream — the remarks cite only Erdős [Er32] (the all-gaps-equal-1 case: 1 is not a sum of reciprocals of consecutive integers) and a conditional reduction to a prime-pair statement. I established the frontier myself this session: no counterexample with max element <= 30000 (scratchpad p287b.py, ~2 min single core).
nodes.search_space_estimate: Cost is NOT the obstacle: one linear sieve per candidate top element b, ~b log log b ops, so b <= 1e9 is ~1e10 ops. The exponential fallback (Fibonacci-many independent subsets T, ~1.618^{b-a}) is never reached — it was needed for 0 of the 30000 values of b I scanned.
nodes.smallest_untested_case: None below b = 30000. I closed b <= 36 by exhaustive exact DFS over Fractions (0 counterexamples) and refuted every 37 <= b <= 30000 by the p-adic forced-exclusion sieve. Smallest genuinely untested case is max element b = 30001.
nodes.statement_short: If 1 = 1/n_1 + ... + 1/n_k with 1<n_1<...<n_k distinct, must max(n_{i+1}-n_i) >= 3?
nodes.upstream_handle: FALSIFIABLE — "Open, but could be disproved with a finite counterexample" (erdosproblems.com/287)
nodes.verdict_reason: Fails criterion 4 for the opposite of the usual reason: the finite search is trivially cheap but empty. For any prime p in [a,b] with floor(b/p)=m small, every multiple of p must be EXCLUDED from S (no nonempty subsum of 1/1..1/m has numerator divisible by p once p > m·lcm(1..m)), yet the excluded set may contain no two consecutive integers. Two forced-adjacent exclusions kill the interval, and that fires for every b in [37, 30000] I tested, with growing slack. This is exactly the page's own remark that a prime p in [N,2N] with (p+1)/2 prime settles it. The residual obstruction is a twin-prime-strength theorem, not compute — no amount of searching produces a witness.
nodes.what_a_witness_is: Concrete: a finite set S of integers with min a, max b, every consecutive gap <= 2, and sum of reciprocals exactly 1. Equivalently S = [a,b] \ T where T contains no two consecutive integers. Verification is one exact rational sum — trivially cheap and exact.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: None recorded. Upstream reports only Cambie's examples for the RELAXED (pairwise-coprime, not prime) version, e.g. 1 = (1+1/5)(1/2+1/3) and 1 = (1+1/41)(1/2+1/3+1/7); and that no example of even the relaxed version is known if 1 is excluded from P and Q. Asked by Barbeau [Ba76]; problem is from [ErGr80].
nodes.search_space_estimate: Capping at the first 100 primes (already an unjustified cap — nothing bounds the largest prime) gives 3^100 ~ 5e47 assignments of each prime to P / Q / neither, and any subset must have >= 60 elements. 35 orders of magnitude past budget.
nodes.smallest_untested_case: Not pinnable. The only hard constraint is |P union Q| >= 60 (from AM-GM: the product being 1 forces sum_{P union Q} 1/p >= 2, and reaching 2 needs the first ~59 primes). No upper bound on the largest prime is known, so there is no well-defined 'next case'.
nodes.statement_short: Are there finite sets of primes P,Q with (sum_{p in P} 1/p)(sum_{q in Q} 1/q) = 1?
nodes.upstream_handle: VERIFIABLE — "Open, but could be proved with a finite example" (erdosproblems.com/307)
nodes.verdict_reason: Passes criteria 1 and 3 (concrete witness, exact cheap check) and fails 2 catastrophically. The search space is not merely large, it is UNBOUNDED — there is no known bound on the largest prime that could appear, so no finite enumeration is ever a complete search. The |P union Q| >= 60 floor guarantees the smallest possible witness already has 60+ primes, so even a bounded heuristic hunt starts at 3^60 ~ 4e28. Nobody has recorded any search at all, which is a signal about tractability, not an opening.
nodes.what_a_witness_is: Concrete: two disjoint finite lists of primes. Verification is one exact rational multiply — cheap and exact.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: Laishram & Shorey 2006 (Int. J. Number Theory 2, 207-215) verified Grimm for ALL n <= 1.9x10^10 — ~1 week of Mathematica on a 2.4 GHz Xeon / 2.5 GB, reduced to checking prime indices N <= 8.5x10^8. Theory bounds: Grimm k << log n/loglog n; Erdos-Selfridge k <= (1+o(1))log n; Ramachandra-Shorey-Tijdeman [RST75] k << (log n/loglog n)^3. Nobody has published past 1.9x10^10 in 20 years.

nodes.verdict_reason: Witness is concrete and verification is exact (trial-division factorisation of <=10^3 integers + Hopcroft-Karp matching, integer-only), but criteria 2 and 4 both fail. Grimm implies p_{n+1}-p_n < p_n^{1/2-c}, i.e. it is STRICTLY HARDER than Legendre's conjecture — a counterexample would require a composite run far longer than Cramer permits. nodes.what_a_witness_is: Concrete. A pair (n,k) such that n+1,...,n+k are all composite and the bipartite graph (interval elements vs. their prime divisors) has NO perfect matching — certified by a Hall-violating subset S of the interval with |union of prime divisors of S| < |S|.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: Berndt & Galway 2000: n < 10^9. Matson 2017 (unsolvedproblems.org S73, quadratic-residue method): n < 10^12. Epstein & Glickman 2020: n <= 10^15, optimised multi-core C++. Theory: Overholt 1993 — finitely many solutions under weak ABC; Naciri 2025 — finitely many if x±1 is k-free or a prime power, and n=4,5,7 only if x±1 is 7-free.
nodes.search_space_estimate: The QR sieve requires primes p > n (for n >= p, n! ≡ 0 mod p and n!+1 ≡ 1 is always a QR — no information), so each prime costs one modular multiply per n: pushing 10^15 -> 10^16 is ~10^16 modmuls per prime and ~50 primes to kill all survivors = ~5x10^17 modular multiplications. Not a one-workstation job by ~3 orders of magnitude.
nodes.smallest_untested_case: n = 10^15 + 1. nodes.verdict_reason: The witness hunt is a WALL (needs a prime gap ~10^6 times longer than anything Cramer permits — it is Legendre in disguise). But this is the one entry where the NEGATIVE certificate is genuinely cheap, monotone and unpublished: 'verified for all k with p_k < 10^18' is a dependency-free integer-only frontier statement, ~1 hour of compute, and upstream lists no range at all. nodes.what_a_witness_is: Concrete and tiny. Reformulation (verified by us): [1..p_{k+1}-1]/[1..p_k] = product of q over all perfect prime powers q^j (j>=2) lying in the gap (p_k, p_{k+1}). So a witness is a single prime gap whose contained prime powers have base-product >= p_k. Since q^2 > p_k forces q > sqrt(p_k), ANY gap containing two prime squares is a counterexample.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: True for all t <= 12 (Costa-Pellegrini 2020, arXiv 2003.05939; literature also states 'true for subsets of size k<=11 in cyclic groups of prime order'). True for p-3 <= t <= p-1 (Hicks-Ollis-Schmitt). Asymptotic ranges: t <= log p/loglog p [Kr24]; t <= e^{c(log p)^{1/4}} [BeKr24]; t <= e^{c(log p)^{1/3}} [CoDe26]; 1 <<_alpha t <= p^{1-alpha} [PhSa26]; p^{1-c} <= t <= (1-o(1))p [BBKMM25]; t >= (1-o(1))p [MuPo25].
nodes.search_space_estimate: A complete sweep of ONE prime is 2^{p-1}/(p-1) sets after the scaling symmetry: p=31 -> 2^30/30 = 3.6x10^7 sets; p=37 -> 2^36/36 = 1.9x10^9; p=41 -> 3.6x10^10. Measured per-set cost (our Python backtracker, t=13, p=17): 4.4 sets/s worst case, i.e. ~0.22 s/set — even a 1000x C speedup leaves p=37 at ~10^5 s. And p is unbounded, so NO sweep ever closes t=13.

'Proved for all sufficiently large p' is assembled from four theorems whose constants are unspecified or ineffective (c in e^{c(log p)^{1/3}}, the <<_alpha in Pham-Sauermann, the o(1) in BBKMM/MuPo), so no explicit p_0 exists and the 'finite check' cannot be enumerated. Exactly the Sendov n_0 = exp(10^126) failure mode we already logged. Meanwhile the small-p end (t<=12, and prime orders up to the literature's computational reach) is already swept, so criteria 2 and 4 both fail. nodes.known_computational_frontier: No published sweep for THIS version. The counterexamples that exist (Cambie's A = primes <= n with m=2n; the concrete ones by Alexeev and Aristotle; the widely-reported Nov-2025 'AI disproved Erdos 488') are all against the [Er61] variant with a∤n instead of a|n, which is believed a typo — upstream restated the problem afterwards. nodes.search_space_estimate: An exhaustive sweep of all A ⊆ [1,24] is 2^24 = 1.7x10^7 sets x an ~8000-term sieve = 1.3x10^11 ops ~ 1 workstation-day. But the extremal family is A={a}, n=2a-1, m=2a giving ratio (2a-1)/a -> 2 as a -> infinity — i.e. the reachable sweep direction (small max(A)) is precisely where the ratio is SMALLEST.

Our sweep this session: ALL A ⊆ [1,14] with |A| <= 4 (1,470 sets, x <= 4000) plus 74,041 random A with |A| <= 8 and max(A) <= 120 (x <= 8000). Max ratio found: 1.991667 at the singleton A={120}, m=240 (n=239). Best non-singleton: 1.849 at A={13,14}. Zero counterexamples.

nodes.what_a_witness_is: Concrete and small: a triple (A, n, m) with m > n >= max(A) violating the inequality. Verified by inclusion-exclusion over subsets of A using floor(x/lcm(S)) — exact integer arithmetic, no floats needed (compare cross-multiplied integers).

nodes.what_a_witness_is: Two very different objects, and they must not be conflated. Criterion 3 passes (tree-containment is exact, integer, dependency-free) and criterion 1 passes, but criterion 2 fails by five orders of magnitude at the first genuinely open cell (~1e17 ops) and — more fundamentally — the search space has no finite bottom. nodes.what_a_witness_is: A graph G with ω(G) < χ(G) = 6 that is not (2,5)-splittable. Usefully, non-(2,5)-splittability collapses by monotonicity to a finite local check: for EVERY edge uv, χ(G − u − v) ≤ 4. So the witness is G plus (i) a 6-colouring, (ii) a DRAT/UNSAT certificate that G has no 5-colouring, (iii) an explicit 4-colouring of G − u − v for each of the |E| edges. Concrete — but there is no bound of any kind on |V(G)|.

nodes.what_a_witness_is: CONCRETE. A finite simple graph G with delta(G) >= 3 whose cycle-length set omits every power of two >= 4. Delivered as an adjacency matrix / graph6 string. The tractable sub-case: a CUBIC graph on 30 vertices with no C4, no C8, no C16 (32 > 30, so only three forbidden lengths). Markström's own reduction (Congr. Numer. 171 (2004)) shows a minimal counterexample has its degree->=4 vertices forming an independent set, and arXiv:2605.22844 (2026) strengthens this to ">= 4/7 of the vertices have degree exactly 3" — both point the search at the cubic lane.

nodes.verdict_reason: Criteria 1 and 3 pass cleanly, criterion 4 fails hard and 2 fails by ~10×. The frontier moved to 6.16×10^17 in June 2026 with a public, laptop-reproducible certificate — we would be re-treading someone else's two-month-old work at 10× the cost. Worse, the object is receding: the required slack is Δ(n) ≤ 2 and the *minimum* observed slack up to 10^12 is 224, with a fitted growth Δ ≈ 0.069(log m)^2.18 — i.e. the data confirms Erdős's own conjecture that max_{m<n}(τ(m)+m−n) → ∞. The surviving candidates are pinned inside admissible prime 7-tuple families, so existence is Schinzel Hypothesis H territory, not a search question. Do not spend compute here.
nodes.what_a_witness_is: A single integer n > 24. Checked by sieving τ(m) for all m < n and confirming the running maximum of m+τ(m) never exceeds n+2. Equivalently τ(n−k) ≤ k+2 for every k ≥ 1, and only k ≲ max τ matters.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: There is no computational frontier — the results are theorems, not searches. Euler (k=4, ℓ=2); Obláth [Ob51] for (k,ℓ)=(5,2),(3,3),(3,4),(3,5); Bennett–Bruin–Győry–Hajdu [BBGH06] for 4 ≤ k ≤ 11; Győry–Hajdu–Pintér [GHP09] for 4 ≤ k ≤ 34 and all ℓ; Bennett–Siksek [BeSi20] for all large k with prime ℓ > e^{10^k}; Marszalek [Ma85] gives k ≪_d 1 for fixed d.

nodes.verdict_reason: Criterion 2 fails absolutely: 'verifiable' here means only that if an example exists it is a finite tuple, not that it lives anywhere findable. Nothing bounds n or d, and Marszalek's k ≪_d 1 is the wrong direction (it bounds k given d, ineffectively for our purposes). The whole 50-year Baker/modularity line — Erdős–Selfridge, Obláth, BBGH, GHP, Bennett–Siksek — points at non-existence, so a search is hunting an object the theory says is not there in a space with no boundary. This is a Diophantine-theory problem wearing a finite-witness costume.

nodes.what_a_witness_is: A triple (n, i, j) with 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n/2 such that no prime p ≥ i divides both C(n,i) and C(n,j). Verified by Kummer's theorem — p | C(n,k) iff adding k and n−k in base p produces a carry — so the check is pure exact integer arithmetic on base-p digits, with no big-integer factoring and no floating point.

nodes.known_computational_frontier: There is no published exhaustive search frontier to beat -- this is the point. The advances are all theorems: Guo-Sun 2005 (an odd squarefree covering would need at least 22 distinct primes; now moot), Hough-Nielsen 2019 (Ann. of Math., every distinct covering has a modulus divisible by 2 or 3), BBMST 2022 'Covering systems with odd moduli' (Discrete Math., simpler proof plus the 9-or-15 lcm condition, and the full squarefree case). nodes.statement_short: Is there a distinct covering system all of whose moduli are odd? A covering system is a finite set of congruences a_i mod n_i, all n_i distinct and > 1, such that every integer satisfies at least one. Asked by Erdos and Selfridge (sometimes with Schinzel).

That is exactly the 'witness not representable' wall reason already recorded on our covering-system boards #2 and #27 ('a min-modulus-40+ covering system already has > 10^50 recursively-defined congruences; no flat poly-time …[truncated; see source]
nodes.what_a_witness_is: NOT CONCRETE IN PRACTICE. Nominally a finite list of pairs (a_i, n_i) with distinct odd n_i > 1 covering Z. But nothing bounds the list length or the moduli, and every structurally comparable object we know of is astronomical: our own atlas boards #2/#27 record that a distinct covering system with minimum modulus 40-42 (Nielsen 2009, Owens 2014) already carries more than 10^50 congruences with an lcm period beyond enumeration. A witness is a recursively-defined construction, not a data file.

nodes.statement_short: The prime power conjecture [Er81]: if a finite projective plane of order n exists must n be a prime power? A plane of order n is a family of (n+1)-subsets of {1,...,n^2+n+1} such that every pair of points lies in exactly one set.

The best exhaustive machinery on this exact graph class (SMS) reaches n = 13 — about 12 orders of magnitude short at n=25, and the theoretical gap runs to a tower of 2's of height 10^14, which is not a number that admits arithmetic.

nodes.statement_short: Murty–Simon conjecture: a diameter-2-critical graph on n vertices (deleting any edge increases the diameter) has at most n²/4 edges, with K_{n/2,n/2} extremal.

The witness is concrete and cheap to check; that is not the problem here.

nodes.verdict_reason: All four criteria hold. (1) A witness is 9 small trees plus an edge assignment — pure integer data. nodes.what_a_witness_is: A counterexample witness is a specific tuple of 9 unlabeled trees (T_2,...,T_10), each given as a parent array / edge list, that admits no edge-disjoint packing into K_10 — accompanied by an exhaustive refutation (search tree). A positive witness (per tuple) is the packing itself: an assignment of each tree's edges to distinct edges of K_10. Note the edge count is exact: sum_{k=2}^{10}(k−1) = 45 = C(10,2), so this is a perfect decomposition, not a packing with slack.

nodes.statement_short: Is there k>2 such that the k-subsets of {1,...,2k} can be coloured with k+1 colours so that every (k+1)-subset sees all k+1 colours among its k-subsets? Equivalently: is chi(J(2k,k)) = k+1 for some k>2, where J(2k,k) is the Johnson graph (k-sets adjacent iff they meet in k-1 elements)? Erdos-Rosenfeld [Er74d, p.283]; k+1 <= chi(J(2k,k)) <= 2k always.

The VERIFIABLE handle only fires in the direction of EXISTENCE, and every data point says no such k exists: chi(J(2k,k)) already runs 2-3 above k+1 by k=7,8, and Ma-Tang shows the only survivors are a thin prime-indexed subsequence they could not reach. So a witness hunt is a hunt for an object nobody believes is there. Settling the smallest live case k=10 the other way (chi(J(20,10)) > 11) is a 2.03M-variable / 101.6M-clause UNSAT with a 20!-sized automorphism group -- not a one-workstation job, and a symmetry-prescribed search that comes back …[truncated; see source]
nodes.what_a_witness_is: CONCRETE. An explicit proper (k+1)-colouring of J(2k,k): a map from the C(2k,k) k-subsets of [2k] into {1,...,k+1} with no two sets meeting in exactly k-1 elements getting the same colour. Equivalently a partition of all k-subsets into k+1 constant-weight codes of length 2k, weight k, minimum Hamming distance 4. Storable as C(2k,k) bytes (184,756 bytes at k=10).

nodes.notes: Round-2 node; RESOLVES the quarantined pending-rename 'generalized_subalgebra_jc'. JC(m,n,k) => JC_m per m (dimension_preserving), so the whole family is refuted for m>=3 (every n>=m); JC(1,n,k) is a theorem (Ayad 2002) and JC(2,n,k) is open with plane JC.
nodes.primary_source: P. Jedrzejewicz & J. Zielinski, Analogs of Jacobian conditions for subrings, J. Pure Appl. Algebra 221 (2017) 2111-2118; arXiv:1601.01508 (Lemma 1.1)
nodes.statement: JC(m,n,k): for f_1..f_m in k[x_1..x_n] (char 0, m<=n), if the gcd of all m-by-m Jacobian minors is a nonzero constant, then k[f_1..f_m] is a ring of constants of a k-derivation. By Lemma 1.1, JC(m,n,k) implies the Jacobian Conjecture for m variables; the diagonal m=n is equivalent to JC_m.

nodes.name: Jelonek's Real Jacobian Conjecture (codimension-2 non-properness)
nodes.notes: Computed floor: fails in some finite dimension (the index-shifted route RealJC_2n => JC_n). Fleet hand analysis: the realification R^6 -> R^6 of Alpöge's map is a non-injective local diffeo with non-properness set of real codimension exactly 2, so the conjecture fails at n=6 and all n >= 6 — and the counterexample proves Jelonek's proven codim >= 3 theorem is OPTIMAL: codimension 2 genuinely fails. Open for n in {3, 4, 5}.
nodes.pre_2026_status: open (n >= 3); theorem for n = 2 and for codim >= 3
nodes.primary_source: Z. Jelonek, Geometry of real polynomial mappings, Math. Z. 239 (2002) 321-333
nodes.statement: For Y : R^n -> R^n a polynomial local diffeomorphism with S_Y its set of non-proper points: if codim(S_Y) >= 2 then Y is bijective. Jelonek proved codim >= 3 unconditionally and the n=2 case, and RealJC_2n => JC_n.

nodes.notes: Computed floor: false for at least one compact group (Mathieu's original implication ran through the dimension-mixing cubic reduction). nodes.statement: For K a compact connected Lie group and f, h K-finite functions: if the Haar integral of f^n vanishes for all n >= 1, then the integral of f^n h vanishes for all sufficiently large n. Mathieu proved this conjecture implies JC.

nodes.name: Poisson Conjecture (Adjamagbo–van den Essen)
nodes.notes: Round-2 second-ring node. The CLASSICAL (commutative symplectic) counterpart of the Dixmier conjecture: P_n is the classical limit of the Weyl algebra A_n. Poisson_n <=> Dixmier_n is per-n (dimension_preserving), and Dixmier now reaches the root through a per-n edge as well, so Poisson inherits FALSE FOR ALL n >= 3 (computed). RETRACTED (round 3): the earlier 'REFUTED_SOME_FINITE_DIM floor via Dixmier's dimension-doubling edge' described the withdrawn edge typing. P_1, P_2 survive (P_2 <=> DC_2 => JC_2, open).
nodes.primary_source: K. Adjamagbo & A. van den Essen, On the equivalence of the Jacobian, Dixmier and Poisson Conjectures in any characteristic, arXiv:math/0608009 (2006); Acta Math. Vietnam. 32 (2007)
nodes.statement: Every C-algebra endomorphism of the Poisson algebra P_n = C[x_1..x_n, y_1..y_n] with the canonical symplectic bracket that preserves the bracket is an automorphism. Adjamagbo-van den Essen prove Jacobian, Dixmier and Poisson are equivalent in any characteristic.

predicates.hot-claim: APPLIES(external-claim-replay, problem) iff an ai_claims entry has our_recorded_status in ('open', 'wall', 'movable') — a live claim against a problem we record unresolved is a verification target, never a status change.
predicates.lane-move: APPLIES(<lane>, deep surface) iff problems.json lane not in ('wall',) — the lane field is authoritative (see atlas/lanes.md).
predicates.strike-ranking: Strike tiers, in order: T1 triage TARGET branches; T2 movable boards (stubs status='movable' UNION deep beatable='MOVABLE'); T3 workable gap surfaces (the 'workable' predicate); T4 triage MAYBE branches. Within a tier: witness_feasibility class ('historic' < 'open-easy' < 'plausible' < 'hard'), then problem id ascending. Prize is NEVER a key (standing rule 2).
predicates.trap: TRAP(problem) iff stubs upstream_finite_handle is set AND stubs status == 'wall' — upstream says a finite object could settle it, our status register records a wall. That wall may be BRANCH-SCOPED: a triage surface on the same card can carry a live TARGET/MAYBE sub-branch (#64 is exactly this). The predicate reads the two registers and nothing else; the reason lives in atlas/walls.md and on the surfaces. The prize rides ON the edge so renderers must show temptation and trap together.
predicates.triage-move: APPLIES(finite-witness-search, triage surface) iff finite_handle_triage verdict in ('TARGET', 'MAYBE').
predicates.workable: APPLIES(witness-local-search, gap surface) iff status == 'open' AND witness_side != 'none' AND witness_feasibility in ('open-easy', 'plausible') — imported from tools/state_of_frontier.is_workable, never forked.

standing_rules: A claim never sets a status: graph statuses are byte-equal to atlas/stubs.json.
Prizes are history, not targets: a prize renders beside its trap warning, never as a ranking key.
Walls render before temptation: every card opens with STOP; sorties opens with DO-NOT-SPEND.
Only cited-implication edges feed propagation; LLM/embedding suggestions stay in quarantine.json at zero weight.
Link-only problems carry no statement text (licensing firewall: no erdosproblems.com prose).
